author: Fable (autonomous)
motivation: SONIC release checkpoint untrained scores 97.39 clean / 69.61 dr_full; every fine-tuned arm is below it (off@32 83.01 clean, off@128 66.67). Fine-tuning at 128 envs is net-destructive with no DR. Trainer facts: checkpoint= loads policy/value weights only (fresh Adam); adaptive-KL LR ended pinned at the floor 1e-5 (per-update KL persistently > 0.02) -> updates are too large for a converged policy, not the LR too high.

design.arm: off (no DR) so the effect is fine-tuning alone
design.origin: settled step-24 (itself already degraded from the release)

hypotheses.H_S1: at least one cell holds id_clean >= 95 (within 2.4 pts of the release) — fine-tuning can be made non-destructive without changing the objective
hypotheses.H_S2: C2 (smaller updates) retains more than C1 (bigger batches) — update magnitude, not sample count, is the driver
hypotheses.H_S3: C3 alone does not reach 95 — entropy drift is a symptom, not the cause

decision_rule: the best cell by id_clean (ties: fewer changed knobs) becomes the fine-tuning regime; then rerun off/fixed/lucid/ta_lucid_50 under it at 32 and 128 it. Do not combine cells post hoc without a new preregistration.
